form.problem: A person with diabetes may have a referral and previous reports but still arrive at hospital without knowing which clinic will receive them or whether a suitable doctor is available. Staff then spend time redirecting patients, checking papers and coordinating appointments across desks and phone calls. These arrangements could begin while the patient is still at home. After the consultation, return dates and missed visits are often tracked separately, leaving care teams to discover travel, work or language barriers through repeated calls. Vishwas addresses this coordination gap for patients, caregivers and hospital teams: getting an existing referral into the correct department's queue before arrival, arranging the appointment and keeping the next visit visible.
form.solution: Vishwas starts with a short enquiry from home: the department named in an existing referral, uploaded documents, language and appointment preferences. Published routing rules send the request to that department's inbox; an unclear referral goes to a coordination inbox. After the department accepts once, Vishwas assigns an available doctor and schedules a compatible slot with the patient's consent. The patient receives the appointment, location and preparation checklist before travelling. A configurable hospital connector exchanges directories, availability and booking acknowledgements. Uploaded files stay encrypted off-chain; an optional Hyperledger Fabric record holds only a salted verification commitment. After the visit, clinician-set return dates drive reminders, barrier handling and attendance tracking. The demo uses fictional patients, a sample hospital API and simulated messaging. Vishwas does not interpret records, diagnose, recommend tests or treatment, or infer a specialty from symptoms.
form.technology: We use a JavaScript web app, Node.js 22 and encrypted SQLite storage. Versioned rules route explicit referrals; deterministic scheduling checks department, language, preferences and capacity. A configurable REST connector integrates a sample hospital API. AES-256-GCM protects records; server sessions enforce access. Hyperledger Fabric stores salted document commitments, with files off-chain. Optional OpenAI drafting supports administrative replies. WhatsApp delivery and ABHA consent remain simulated.

disclosure.clinical_scope: Administrative coordination only; no clinical inference or advice
disclosure.messaging_demo: Simulated WhatsApp inbox; no actual messages sent
disclosure.ai: OpenAI administrative drafting adapter implemented and tested with mocked provider responses; no live credentials configured; template fallback verified
disclosure.security: AES-256-GCM encrypted workflow and documents with server authorization. Real local Fabric anchoring and integrity verification passed. Files and sensitive metadata remain off-chain. Not end-to-end encryption or compliance certification.
disclosure.routing: Explicit referral department or exact directory label only; no medical interpretation. Department accepts once, followed by consented deterministic assignment and scheduling.
disclosure.hospital_connector: Configurable sample API implemented and tested over HTTP, including remote booking acknowledgement. Real vendor mapping and hospital acceptance remain future work.
disclosure.blockchain: A real two-organization local Hyperledger Fabric 2.5.16 network committed and queried salted document commitments. No patient documents, names, IDs or raw file hashes are on-chain. This is a development network, not a hospital consortium.
disclosure.video: Updated 60-second film demonstrates the revised real local flow: one acceptance, sample hospital API acknowledgement, encrypted upload, actual local Fabric verification and confirmed return. Fictional data; no patient outcome claims.

business_model.status: Proposed commercial model; no paying customers, commercial pilot or measured ROI
business_model.model: B2B hospital site subscription; patient and caregiver access free
business_model.buyer: Hospital administrator, owner or operations head
business_model.initial_segment: One diabetes OPD in a mid-size hospital with a care desk and usable scheduling API
business_model.scope: One site, up to three departments and 3,000 new enquiries per month; agreed storage, retention and support terms
business_model.pilot_credit: On conversion within 30 days of evaluation, credit the pilot fee against the first annual subscription; the annual term starts on the pilot start date and includes the pilot period
business_model.first_year_example: 40000 pilot + 200000 subscription balance + 60000 integration = 300000 INR, before approved usage and applicable taxes
business_model.variable_costs: Messaging and vendor API charges separately approved at actual cost or billed directly to hospital
business_model.fabric: Optional, custom-priced shared-network operation only where participating institutions need it
business_model.incentives: No patient routing fee, referral commission, paid doctor ranking or patient data sale
business_model.validation: Paid scoped pilot measures net staff effort, booking turnaround and clinician-planned return attendance before expansion
